## Problem

Checkpoints store session transcripts as a continuous blob (`full.jsonl`, the whole session up to the commit). When a session spans multiple commits, there is no way to know which part of the conversation produced which commit, so a reader of one checkpoint must read the whole session.

## Proposed Solution

1. When creating a checkpoint, record the JSONL line range of the session that occurred since the previous checkpoint of the same session ID (the session file only grows, so line numbers stay stable).
2. Store the range as `scope_start` and `scope_end` fields in checkpoint metadata, with the commit hash of the checkpoint.
3. Add `partio explain <checkpoint-id> --transcript` to print only that segment. `partio explain` (`cmd/partio/explain.go`) already prints the metadata, prompt and context of a checkpoint; `partio rewind` lists and restores, and shows no transcript.

Partio has no transcript compaction, so the original item "compaction preserves scope boundaries" is removed (argos review, 2026-10-10). Related: #423 (the prompt of the turn that made each commit; the scope range gives it), #733 (offset cache for re-redaction).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each checkpoint stores `scope_start` and `scope_end`: the JSONL lines since the previous checkpoint of the same session
- [ ] The first checkpoint of a session starts its scope at line 1
- [ ] `partio explain <checkpoint-id> --transcript` prints only the lines of that scope
- [ ] Checkpoints without scope fields (written before this change) print the whole transcript, with a note

Inspired by entireio/cli 0.8.0 changelog (checkpoints store full compacted transcripts with scope markers)
